whisper.label: Whisper Large-V3
whisper.text:
On June 18, 1999, Martin Richardson collaborated with David Bowie on a silent experimental
film with the aim of using it to create a hologram.
The following includes archive footage of the experimental camera with Martin Richardson
together with his cameraman John Wilcher.
The resulting 35mm film depicted a barefoot Bowie performing a series of his iconic movements
that were often used as stage prompts during live performances to indicate scenery or lighting
change.
These enactments may be traced to Bowie's earlier collaboration in the 1960s with mime
artist Lindsay Kemp, who influenced Bowie's theatrical personas such as Ziggy Stardust
and the Thin White Duke.
These actions were well known to fans that recognized them to be associated to individual songs.
The film was also the first to be released in the United States in the late 1960s.
